Dijital Okuryazarlık Ölçeği: Türkçe ’ye Uyarlama Çalışması 1
Nazire Burçin HAMUTOĞLU 2, Özlem CANAN GÜNGÖREN 3, Gülden KAYA UYANIK4,
Duygu GÜR ERDOĞAN5
Geliş Tarihi: 15.11.2016 Kabul Tarihi: 07.05.2017
Bu çalışmada Ng tarafından 2012 yılında geliştirilen 17 maddeden oluşan “Dijital Okuryazarlık Ölçeğinin” Türkçe ’ye uyarlaması yapılmıştır.
Ölçeğin orijinali 4 faktörlü bir yapıya sahiptir.
Bu faktörler tutum, teknik, bilişsel ve sosyal olarak isimlendirilmiştir.
Ölçeğin Türkçe’ ye uyarlama çalışmaları dilsel eşdeğerlik ile başlamış, iyi derecede İngilizce ve Türkçe bilen 3 uzman tarafından İngilizce'den Türkçe'ye, farklı 3 uzman tarafından da Türkçe'den İngilizce'ye çevrilmiş, uzmanların görüşleri doğrultusunda Türkçe deneme formu elde edilerek İngilizce ve Türkçe bilen 37 akademisyene iki hafta arayla her iki form uygulanmış ve her iki form arasındaki korelasyon katsayıları anlamlı olarak bulunmuştur.
Dilsel eşdeğerliğin ardından AFA, DFA ve güvenirlik analizleri ile gerçekleştirilmiştir.
AFA için 185 öğrenciden elde edilen veriler, DFA için ise farklı 210 öğrenciden elde edilen veriler kullanılmıştır.
Birinci düzey DFA ile araştırma grubundaki kişi sayısı faktör analizi için yeterli seviyede olduğu, ikinci düzey DFA ile dijital okuryazarlık örtük değişkenin anlamlı birer yordayıcısı olduğu bulunmuştur.
İç tutarlılık katsayısı (Cronbach Alpha) ve test tekrar test yöntemleriyle de ölçeğin güvenirliğine bakılmıştır.
Elde edilen bulgular sonucunda ölçeğin Türkçe formunun geçerli ve güvenilir bir yapıya sahip olduğu görülmüştür.
Anahtar Kelimeler: dijital okuryazarlık, ölçek, güvenirlik, geçerlik.

Adapting Digital Literacy Scale into Turkish
Submitted by 15.11.2016 Accepted by 07.05.2017
Abstract
In this study it is aimed to adapt the “Digital Literacy Scale” to Turkish, which was developed by Ng (2012), and included 17 items.
Ege Eğitim Dergisi 2017(18) 1: 408- 429 Dijital Okuryazarlık Ölçeği: Türkçe ’ye Uyarlama Çalışması 410 Giriş
Günümüzde her geçen gün birçok yeni teknoloji ortaya çıkmaktadır.
Bunlar içerisinde ilk
akla gelenler kablosuz internet teknolojileri ile mobil teknolojilerdir.
Özellikle internet
teknolojileri ile birlikte günlük hayatımızda yer eden ve bireylerin farklı amaçlarına
ulaşmasını sağlayacak, bireylere kolaylık sağlayan, çok sayıda web sayfası bulunmaktadır.
Son dönemde bireysel internet kullanımının eğitim, sağlık, iş ve özel sektörlerde
yaygınlaşması göze çarpmaktadır.
Bireylerin Sosyal ağları kullanma, belli bir gruba üye
olma, haber okuma, görüşlerini dile getirme, müzik dinleme, film izleme vb.
gibi birçok faklı
amaçlar doğrultusunda internet kullandığı gözlenmektedir.
Ancak bu web sayfaların hepsi
aynı derece güvenilir olma özelliğine sahip değildir.
Bununla birlikte, internette gezinirken
farklı amaçlara hizmet etmekte olan kullanıcı profili ile karşılaşmak da mümkündür.
Bu web
sayfalarında gezinen bireyler, çevrimiçi hırsızlık, dolandırılma, yanlış yönlendirilme, sanal
zorbalık, kişisel bilgilerin paylaşımı, zararlı yazılımlar istismar vb.
istenmeyen davranışlara
maruz kalabilmektedir (Telekomünikasyon İletişim Başkanlığı, TİB, 2012).
Benzer şekilde,
okuduğumuz bir haberin kaynağının güvenirliği, o konu hakkındaki tavır ve tutumumuzu
belirlemede önemlidir.
Herkes gibi özellikle, ergenlik çağındaki bireyler ile çok fazla internet
deneyimi olmayan bireylerin; internette karşılaştıkları kullanıcı profilleri, gezindikleri
sitelerden elde ettikleri bilgiler ve sosyal ağlarda tanıştıkları bireyler ile iletişimde bulunurken
dikkat etmesi gerekmektedir.
Bu durum bireylerin dijital okuryazarlık becerilerine sahip
olmasını gerekli kılmaktadır.
Farklı teknolojileri kullanarak güvenli internet kullanımını arttırmak, edinilen bilginin
doğru/yanlışlığı hakkında karar verebilmek vb.
becerilere sahip olabilmek için yapılan
çalışmaların yanı sıra; bireylerin karşılaştıkları problemleri çözmede dijital okuryazarlık
becerilerinin önemli olduğu düşünülmektedir.
Aksi durumda, bilginin çok hızlı bir şekilde
yayıldığı günümüzde, güvenirliği düşük, doğruluğu ispatlanmamış, provokasyon amaçlı
yapılan yanlış bilgilendirilmeler bireyler ve toplum açısından yanıltıcı sonuçlar
doğurabilmektedir.
Çubukçu ve Bayzan (2013), internet risklerinin oluşmasındaki en büyük
etkenin doğru olmayan, istismar edici, yanıltıcı bilgilerin üretilmesi ve paylaşılmasından
kaynaklandığını belirtmektedir.
Bu durumda, bireylerin dijital okuryazarlık becerilerinin
öneminin tartışılması kaçınılmazdır (Ainley, Schulz ve Fraillon, 2016; Mohammadyari ve
Singh, 2015).
Ege Eğitim Dergisi 2017(18) 1: 408- 429 Dijital Okuryazarlık Ölçeği: Türkçe ’ye Uyarlama Çalışması 411 Dijital okuryazarlık, dijital vatandaşlığın en önemli ayağını oluşturan boyutlarından
birisidir (Ribble, 2011).
Dijital ortam kullanıcıların sahip olması gereken becerileri
tanımlama çabaları mevcuttur (Burnett ve McKinley, 1998 ; Zins, 2000).
Dijital okuryazarlık,
farklı teknolojilerin doğru kullanılabilmesi ile birlikte doğru bilgiye ulaşma, üretme ve
paylaşımda bulunabilme ve öğrenme-öğretme süreçlerinde teknolojiyi kullanabilme
becerilerine sahip olmayı gerektirmektedir.
Çubukçu ve Bayzan (2013), dijital okuryazarlık
becerileri ile ilgili FATIH Projesi’nin okullardaki eğitim sürecinde önemli bir yeri teşkil
edecek olması ve okullarda Medya Okuryazarlığı dersinin seçmeli verilmeye başlamasını
fırsat olarak değerlendirmektedir.
Dijital ortamlar ile ilgili Avrupa Birliği için hazırlanan
Dijital Okuryazarlık raporunda, “öğrencilerin yaratıcılıkları ile kendilerini ifade etme
becerilerini geliştirdiği” belirtilmektedir (Tornero, 2004).
Yaşanan teknolojik gelişmeler göz önünde bulundurulduğunda, ülkemizde dijital
okuryazarlık becerilerinin ne düzeyde olduğunu belirleyen bir ölçme aracına ihtiyaç olduğu
görülmektedir.
Bu amaca hizmet etmek üzere, Ng (2012) tarafından geliştirilen dijital
okuryazarlık ölçeğinin dilimize ve kültürümüze uyarlanması planlanmaktadır.
21. yüzyıl
bireyleri için, güvenilir bilgiye ulaşma, güvenli internet kullanımı ve bilinçli internet
kullanımı gibi dijital okuryazarlık becerileri önemli görülmektedir.
Literatürde dijital
teknolojilerin kullanılarak okuma- yazma gerçekleştirilmesi ile ilgili yapılan çalışmalar ile
yükseköğretimde dijital okuryazarlığın önemli olduğu ile ilgili çalışmalar mevcuttur (Özbay
ve Özdemir, 2014; Prior, Mazanov, Meacheam, Heaslip ve Hanson, 2016; Radovanović,
Hogan ve Lalić, 2015; Tüzel ve Tok, 2013).
Sönmez ve Gül (2014), dijital çağda bireylerin
karşılaştıkları dijital problemleri çözebilmeleri için, dijital okuryazarlık bilişsel becerilerine
sahip olmaları gerektiğini vurgulamaktadır.
Çubukçu ve Bayzan (2013) dijital okuryazarlığın
bilinen okuryazarlıktan bile daha önemli bir hal almaya başladığını belirtmektedir.
Bu
çalışmalar ışığında eğitimde dijital okuryazarlık becerilerini kazandıracak olan öğretmenlerin
bu konu hakkındaki becerileri önem kazanmaktadır.
Türkiye’de öğretmen adaylarının
internete erişim olanakları ve interneti kullanım amaçları ile ilgili yapılan istatistikler,
öğretmen adaylarının büyük bir çoğunluğunun (%86,9) interneti kullandığını göstermektedir
(Akkoyunlu ve Yılmaz, 2005; Atav, Akkoyunlu ve Sağlam, 2006).
İnternetin yoğun bir
şekilde kullanılmasına rağmen, öğretmen adaylarının dijital okuryazarlık becerilerini ortaya
koyan bir ölçme aracının olmayışı bu çalışmayı önemli kılmaktadır.
Ege Eğitim Dergisi 2017(18) 1: 408- 429 Dijital Okuryazarlık Ölçeği: Türkçe ’ye Uyarlama Çalışması 412 Bu çalışmada dilimize uyarlanan Dijital Okuryazarlık ölçeği, öğretmen adaylarının
hem dijital okuryazarlık becerilerinin belirlenmesi açısından hem de bu becerilerin
geliştirilmesi ile ilgili yapılacak aktivitelere temel oluşturacağından önemli görülmektedir.
Yöntem
Çalışma Grubu
Dijital Okuryazarlık Ölçeğinin geçerlik ve güvenirlik çalışmaları 2015-2016 öğretim yılı
Bahar döneminde Sakarya Üniversitesi Eğitim fakültesinin farklı bölümlerinde okuyan
öğrenciler ile yürütülmüştür.
Araştırmanın örneklemini dört farklı çalışma grubu
oluşturmakla beraber toplam 485 kişi oluşturmaktadır.
İlk grup 20’si ( %54) kadın, 17’si
(%46) erkek olmak üzere toplam 37 akademisyenden oluşmaktadır ve bu grup ile dilsel
eşdeğerlilik çalışması yapılmıştır.
İkinci grup 108’i (%58,4) kadın, 77’si (%41,6) erkek
olmak üzere toplam 185 kişiden oluşmaktadır ve açımlayıcı faktör analizi ile iç tutarlık
çalışmaları bu gruptan elde edilen verilerle gerçekleştirilmiştir.
Üçüncü grup 118 kadın (%
56,2) ve 92 erkek (%43,8) olmak üzere toplam 210 kişiden oluşmaktadır ve doğrulayıcı
faktör analizi sonuçları bu gruptan elde edilmiştir.
Dördüncü grup ise 20 kadın (% 37,7) ve
33 erkek (%62,3) olmak üzere toplam 53 kişiden oluşmaktadır ve bu kişilerden elde edilen
veriler üzerinden ölçeğin test tekrar test analizleri yapılmıştır.
Veri Toplama Aracı: Dijital Okuryazarlık Ölçeği
Dijital Okuryazarlık Ölçeği (DOYÖ) Ng (2012) tarafından geliştirilmiş 17 maddeden ve 4 faktörden
(tutum, teknik, bilişsel ve sosyal) oluşan bir ölçektir.
Ölçeğin orijinali Avustralya’da bulunan bir
üniversitede öğrenim gören, yaşları 18 ile 30 arasında değişen öğretmen adayları üzerinde
uygulanmıştır.
Tersten puanlanan maddenin bulunmadığı ölçekte Kesinlikle Katılıyorum (5),
Kesinlikle Katılmıyorum (1) şeklinde 5’li Likert tipi bir derecelendirme kullanılmıştır.
İşlem
Dijital Okuryazarlık Ölçeğinin Türkçeye uyarlama çalışması öncelikle orijinal dilde ölçeğin
geliştiricisi olan Ng ile iletişime geçilerek ölçeğin uyarlanması için izin alınmasıyla
başlamıştır.
Gerekli izinler sağlandıktan sonra ölçeğin kaynak dil olan İngilizceden hedef dil
olan Türkçeye çeviri süreci başlatılmıştır.
Bir ölçme aracının geliştirildiği toplumdan farklı
bir topluma uyarlanması sırasındaki en önemli işlemi ölçeğin kaynak dilden hedef dile
çevirisi süreci oluşturmaktadır (Geisinger, 1994).
Her iki formun yeteri kadar birbirine
benzediği görüşü alındıktan sonra ölçeğin uygulama hazır, son hali ortaya çıkarılmıştır.
Ölçek
dil geçerliliği için yeterli hale getirilmiştir.
Dilsel eşdeğerliliği çalışmaları 37 akademisyen ile
Ege Eğitim Dergisi 2017(18) 1: 408- 429 Dijital Okuryazarlık Ölçeği: Türkçe ’ye Uyarlama Çalışması 413 iki dilli desen yöntemiyle yürütülmüştür.
Yapı geçerliliği için toplanan veri, veri ön işleme
yöntemleri kullanılarak incelenmiştir (Oğuzlar, 2003).
DOYÖ’nin yapı geçerliliği çalışması
betimleyici faktör analizi (exploratory factor analysis) ve doğrulayıcı faktör analizi
(confirmatory factor analysis) yöntemleri kullanılarak yürütülmüştür.
Faktör analizi
çalışmalarında bazı varsayımsal ölçütlerin aranması gerekmektedir.
Bu amaçla varsayımsal
ölçütler olarak AFA için normal dağılım, doğrusallık, aykırı değerlerin çıkarılması, boş
değerlerin belirlenmesi incelenirken DFA için aranan tüm varsayımsal kriterlerle birlikte
uyum iyiliği indekslerinin yeterlilik düzeyleri incelenmiştir.
DOYÖ’nin uyarlama çalışmasında toplanan verinin yapı geçerliği çalışmaları için
gereken yeterliliği gösterdiği gözlenerek yapı geçerliği çalışması yapılmıştır.
Ölçeğin
güvenirlik düzeyi Cronbach alfa iç tutarlılık ve test tekrar test yöntemleri aracılığıyla
incelenmiştir.
DOYÖ’nin uyarlama çalışmalarında kullanılan tüm istatistiksel analizler SPSS
20.0 ve LISREL 8.7 paket programlarıyla yapılmıştır.

Yapı Geçerliği

Ayrıca ölçeğin yakınsak ve ayırt edici geçerliği de incelenmiştir.
Açımlayıcı Faktör Analizi (AFA)
Açımlayıcı faktör analizi gerçekleştirilmeden önce veri setinin faktör analizi için uygun olup
olmadığının belirlenmesi gerekir.
Örneklemin veri analizine uygun olup olmadığını
belirlemek için yapılacak işlem Kaiser-Meyer-Oklin’in (KMO) ve Barlett Sphericity
testlerinin gerçekleştirilmesidir.
KMO 0 ile 1 arasında değişen değerler alabilmektedir ve
0.5’in üzerindeki KMO değerleri kabul edilebilir değerdir (Field, 2009).
Bununla birlikte; 0.5
ile 0.7 arasındaki KMO değerlerinin orta, 0.7 ile 0.8 arasındaki değerlerin iyi, 0.8 ile 0.9
arasındaki değerlerin çok iyi ve 0.9’un üzerindeki değerlerin ise mükemmel olduğu kabul
edilmektedir (Field, 2009).
Bu çalışmada KMO örneklem uygunluk katsayısı .91, Barlett
Sphericity testi değeri ise 1549.40 (p<.01, sd=136) bulunmuştur.
Bu sonuca göre, verilerin
faktör analizine mükemmel uygunlukta olduğu söylenebilir.
AFA’da temel bileşenler
yöntemi (principal components) ve varimax döndürme tekniği kullanılmıştır.
Temel
bileşenler yöntemi bağımlılık yapısını yok etme amacıyla tanıma, sınıflandırma, boyut
indirgenme ve yorumlanmasını sağlayan, çok değişkenli bir istatistiksel yöntemdir (Jolliffe,
2002).
Buna göre AFA sonucunda toplam varyansın %65.78’ini açıklayan ve orijinal
formdaki maddelerle bire bir örtüşen 4 faktörlü bir yapı elde edilmiştir (Şekil 1).

Bu çalışmada

Goodness), iyilik uyum indeksi (Goodness of Fit Index, GFI), düzeltilmiş iyilik uyum indeksi

In this study, the adaptation of the “Digital Literacy Scale,” developed by Ng in 2012 and consisting of 17 items, into Turkish was carried out. The original scale has a four-factor structure. These factors are named as attitude, technical, cognitive, and social. The adaptation process into Turkish began with linguistic equivalence; three experts who were highly proficient in both English and Turkish translated the scale from English to Turkish, and another three experts translated it from Turkish to English. Based on the experts’ opinions, a Turkish trial form was created, and both the English and Turkish versions were administered to 37 academics proficient in both languages, with two weeks between each administration. The correlation coefficients between the two forms were found to be significant. After establishing linguistic equivalence, EFA, CFA, and reliability analyses were conducted. Data obtained from 185 students were used for EFA, and data from a separate group of 210 students were used for CFA. The first-order CFA showed that the sample size was sufficient for factor analysis, and the second-order CFA demonstrated that digital literacy is a significant predictor of the latent variables. The reliability of the scale was assessed using internal consistency coefficients (Cronbach's Alpha) and test-retest methods. As a result of the findings, it was observed that the Turkish form of the scale has a valid and reliable structure. Abstract  
In this study, it is aimed to adapt the “Digital Literacy Scale,” developed by Ng (2012) and consisting of 17 items, into Turkish. Ege Education Journal 2017(18) 1: 408-429 Digital Literacy Scale: Turkish Adaptation Study 410 Introduction  
Today, many new technologies are emerging every day. Among the foremost of these are wireless internet technologies and mobile technologies. Especially with internet technologies, numerous websites that facilitate daily life and enable individuals to achieve various goals have become an integral part of our lives. Recently, the widespread use of personal internet access in education, health, business, and the private sector has become notable. It is observed that individuals use the internet for a variety of purposes such as using social networks, joining specific groups, reading news, expressing their opinions, listening to music, watching movies, and similar activities. However, not all of these web pages possess the same degree of reliability. However, it is also possible to encounter different user profiles serving various purposes while browsing the internet. Individuals browsing these web pages may encounter online theft, fraud, misguidance, cyberbullying, sharing of personal information, exploitation by malicious software, etc. They may be exposed to undesirable behaviors (Telecommunications Communication Presidency, TIB, 2012). Similarly, the reliability of the source of a news article we read is important in determining our attitude and stance on that subject. Like everyone else, individuals—especially adolescents and those with limited internet experience—need to be cautious when interacting with the user profiles they encounter online, the information they obtain from the websites they browse, and the people they meet on social networks. This situation necessitates that individuals possess digital literacy skills. In addition to efforts aimed at increasing safe internet usage through different technologies and acquiring skills such as being able to determine the accuracy of the information obtained, digital literacy skills are also considered important for individuals in solving the problems they encounter. Otherwise, in today's world where information spreads very rapidly, misinformation with low reliability, unverifiable accuracy, and intended for provocation can lead to misleading outcomes for individuals and society. Çubukçu and Bayzan (2013) state that the greatest factor in the emergence of internet risks is the production and sharing of false, exploitative, and misleading information. In this regard, discussing the importance of individuals' digital literacy skills becomes inevitable (Ainley, Schulz, and Fraillon, 2016; Mohammadyari and Singh, 2015). Ege Education Journal 2017(18) 1: 408–429 Digital Literacy Scale: Adaptation to Turkish 411 Digital literacy is one of the essential dimensions that constitute the most important pillar of digital citizenship (Ribble, 2011). There are efforts to define the skills that digital environment users should possess (Burnett and McKinley, 1998; Zins, 2000). Digital literacy requires possessing the skills to use various technologies correctly, to access, produce, and share accurate information, and to utilize technology in learning and teaching processes. Çubukçu and Bayzan (2013) consider the significance of digital literacy skills in that the FATIH Project will hold an important place in the school education process, and that the introduction of the Media Literacy course as an elective in schools is regarded as an opportunity. In the Digital Literacy report prepared for the European Union regarding digital environments, it is stated that “students develop their creativity and self-expression skills” (Tornero, 2004). Considering the technological developments experienced, it is observed that there is a need for a measurement tool to determine the level of digital literacy skills in our country. To serve this purpose, it is planned to adapt the digital literacy scale developed by Ng (2012) into our language and culture. For 21st-century individuals, digital literacy skills such as accessing reliable information, safe internet use, and conscious internet use are considered important. In the literature, there are studies related to conducting reading and writing using digital technologies as well as studies that highlight the importance of digital literacy in higher education (Özbay and Özdemir, 2014; Prior, Mazanov, Meacheam, Heaslip, and Hanson, 2016; Radovanović, Hogan, and Lalić, 2015; Tüzel and Tok, 2013). Sönmez and Gül (2014) emphasize that in order for individuals to solve the digital problems they encounter in the digital age, they need to possess cognitive skills of digital literacy. Çubukçu and Bayzan (2013) state that digital literacy has begun to become even more important than conventional literacy. In light of these studies, the skills of teachers, who are responsible for imparting digital literacy abilities in education, gain significant importance. Statistics on prospective teachers’ access to the internet and their purposes for using it in Türkiye indicate that the vast majority of prospective teachers (86.9%) use the internet (Akkoyunlu and Yılmaz, 2005; Atav, Akkoyunlu, and Sağlam, 2006). Despite this intensive use of the internet, the absence of a measurement tool to reveal prospective teachers’ digital literacy skills makes this study significant. In this study, the adaptation of the Digital Literacy Scale into Turkish is considered important, as it will serve not only to determine the digital literacy skills of prospective teachers but also to provide a basis for activities aimed at developing these skills. Method
Study Group
The validity and reliability studies of the Digital Literacy Scale were conducted during the Spring semester of the 2015-2016 academic year with students from different departments of the Faculty of Education at Sakarya University. Although the sample of the study consisted of four different working groups, a total of 485 individuals participated. The first group consisted of 37 academics—20 (54%) women and 17 (46%) men—and linguistic equivalence studies were conducted with this group. The second group comprised 185 people—108 (58.4%) women and 77 (41.6%) men—and data from this group were used for exploratory factor analysis and internal consistency studies. The third group consisted of 210 people—118 (56.2%) women and 92 (43.8%) men—and confirmatory factor analysis results were obtained from this group. The fourth group included 53 people—20 (37.7%) women and 33 (62.3%) men—and test-retest analyses of the scale were conducted using data obtained from this group. Data Collection Tool: Digital Literacy Scale  
The Digital Literacy Scale (DLS) was developed by Ng (2012) and consists of 17 items and 4 factors (attitude, technical, cognitive, and social). The original scale was administered to prospective teachers aged between 18 and 30 studying at a university in Australia. The scale does not contain any reverse-scored items and uses a 5-point Likert scale ranging from Strongly Agree (5) to Strongly Disagree (1).  
Procedure  
The process of adapting the Digital Literacy Scale into Turkish began with obtaining permission to adapt the scale from its developer, Ng, in the original language. Once the necessary permissions were obtained, the translation process from the source language, English, to the target language, Turkish, was initiated. The most important step in adapting a measurement tool from one society to another is the translation process from the source language to the target language (Geisinger, 1994). After it was confirmed that both versions were sufficiently similar, the final draft of the scale became ready for implementation. The scale was made adequate for language validity. Linguistic equivalence studies were carried out using the bilingual design method with 37 academicians.  
For construct validity, the collected data were examined using data preprocessing methods (Oğuzlar, 2003). The construct validity study of the DLS was conducted using exploratory factor analysis (EFA) and confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) methods. Certain hypothetical criteria are required for factor analysis studies. For this purpose, in EFA, assumptions such as normality, linearity, removal of outliers, and identification of missing values were examined, while in CFA, all required hypothetical criteria were investigated along with the adequacy levels of goodness-of-fit indices.  
It was observed that the data collected for the adaptation study of the DLS met the requisite adequacy for construct validity, and thus, a construct validity study was conducted. The reliability level of the scale was examined using Cronbach's alpha internal consistency and test-retest methods. All statistical analyses used in the adaptation studies of the DLS were conducted using the SPSS 20.0 and LISREL 8.7 software packages. Findings  
Linguistic Equivalence  
The linguistic equivalence study of the Digital Literacy Scale (DLS) was conducted with 37 participants. According to the findings, the correlation coefficients between the scores of the Turkish and original English forms were found to be .89 for the whole scale, .80 for the Attitude subscale, .93 for the Technical subscale, .73 for the Cognitive subscale, and .73 for the Social subscale. Exploratory Factor Analysis (EFA) and Confirmatory Factor Analysis (CFA) were conducted to examine the factor structure of the Turkish form of the DLS. In addition, the convergent and discriminant validity of the scale were also investigated. Exploratory Factor Analysis (EFA)
Before conducting exploratory factor analysis, it is necessary to determine whether the data set is suitable for factor analysis. The procedures to determine whether the sample is appropriate for data analysis are the implementation of the Kaiser-Meyer-Olkin (KMO) and Bartlett’s Sphericity tests. The KMO can take values ranging from 0 to 1, and KMO values above 0.5 are considered acceptable (Field, 2009). Moreover, KMO values between 0.5 and 0.7 are considered moderate, values between 0.7 and 0.8 are considered good, values between 0.8 and 0.9 are considered very good, and values over 0.9 are regarded as excellent (Field, 2009). In this study, the KMO sample adequacy coefficient was found to be .91, and the Bartlett’s Sphericity test value was 1549.40 (p<.01, df=136). According to these results, it can be said that the data are in excellent conformity for factor analysis. In EFA, the principal components method and varimax rotation technique were used. The principal components method is a multivariate statistical technique that enables identification, classification, dimensionality reduction, and interpretation, and aims to remove the dependence structure (Jolliffe, 2002). Accordingly, as a result of the EFA, a four-factor structure was obtained that accounts for 65.78% of the total variance and exactly matches the items in the original form (Figure 1). Figure 1. Confirmatory Factor Analysis (CFA)
In this study, CFA was conducted to determine whether the factor structure of the original form of the DLS could be confirmed in the Turkish sample. In this context, to evaluate the adequacy of the model tested in CFA, the Chi-Square Goodness of Fit Test, Goodness of Fit Index (GFI), Adjusted Goodness of Fit Index (AGFI), Comparative Fit Index (CFI), Normed Fit Index (NFI), Non-Normed Fit Index (NNFI), Root Mean Square Error of Approximation (RMSEA), and Standardized Root Mean Square Residual (SRMR) were examined. The criteria to be considered regarding the fit indices are generally as follows: for GFI, CFI, and NFI, a value of 0.90 indicates acceptable fit, while a value of 0.95 indicates perfect fit. (Bentler, 1980; Bentler and Bonett, 1980; Marsh, Hau, Artelt, Baumert, and Peschar, 2006). For NNFI, a value of .95 is considered an acceptable fit criterion and a value of .97 is considered an excellent fit criterion. For AGFI, a value of .85 indicates acceptable fit, and a value of .90 indicates excellent fit (Schermelleh-Engel and Moosbrugger, 2003). For RMSEA, a value of .08 indicates acceptable fit and .05 indicates excellent fit (Brown and Cudeck, 1993; Byrne and Campbell, 1999). For SRMR, a value of .05 is considered an excellent fit and a value of .10 is considered an acceptable fit criterion (Schermelleh-Engel and Moosbrugger, 2003). The fit indices of the model obtained in the CFA were examined, and it was found that the minimum chi-square value (χ2=268.45, df=113, p=0.00) was significant. The fit index values were found to be RMSEA = .071, GFI = .93, AGFI = .91, CFI = .98, NFI = .96, NNFI = .97, and SRMR = .05. Therefore, it can be said that the Attitude, Technical, Cognitive, and Social subscales are significant predictors of the latent variable of digital literacy. Convergent and discriminant validity
To determine the construct validity of whether the Digital Literacy Scale measures a four-factor structure, convergent and discriminant validity were examined. For convergent validity, the Average Variance Extracted (AVE) values for each factor were analyzed. The AVE values for each factor were found to be 0.62, 0.58, 0.52, and 0.61, respectively. It is stated that all of these values being above .50 provides evidence for convergent validity (Bagozzi and Yi, 1988). The discriminant validity was assessed by examining whether the square roots of the AVE values of the scales were greater than both the correlations between the constructs and the value of 0.70 (Fornell and Larcker, 1981), and it was found that the scale possesses discriminant validity (Table 5). In the study, the internal consistency coefficient obtained from 185 students was calculated as .93 for the entire scale. The internal consistency coefficients for the subscales were found to be .88 for the Attitude subscale, .89 for the Technical subscale, .70 for the Cognitive subscale, and .72 for the Social subscale. In order to determine the test-retest reliability of the Digital Literacy Scale, the scale was administered to 53 students from the departments of Computer Education and Technology Teaching twice, with a three-week interval, and the correlations between the two administrations were calculated. The reliability coefficients calculated using the test-retest method were .98 for the entire scale, .89 for the Attitude subscale, .90 for the Technical subscale, .87 for the Cognitive subscale, and .79 for the Social subscale. Scales with a reliability coefficient of .70 or above are considered reliable (Büyüköztürk, 2010; Pallant, 2005; Tezbaşaran, 1996). Accordingly, it can be stated that the reliability coefficients of the overall scale as well as its Attitude, Technical, Cognitive, and Social subscales are at a sufficient level. Evaluation of Scores Obtained from the DLS  
The DLS consists of 17 items. A 5-point Likert-type rating is used in the scale, ranging from Strongly Agree (5) to Strongly Disagree (1). There are no reverse-scored items on the scale. The scale consists of four dimensions: attitude, technical, cognitive, and social. Since the Attitude subscale contains 7 items, the minimum score that can be obtained from this dimension is 7, and the maximum is 35. The Technical subscale consists of 6 items; therefore, the minimum possible score for this dimension is 6, and the maximum is 30. The Cognitive subscale contains 2 items; thus, the minimum score is 2 and the maximum is 10. Similarly, the Social subscale also consists of 2 items, and the minimum and maximum possible scores are 2 and 10, respectively. The fact that the DLS provides sufficient fit indices in both the first and second order CFAs indicates that it is possible to work with scores obtained from the subscales, as well as to obtain an overall score for digital literacy from the scale. Higher scores obtained from the subscales and the overall scale of the DLS indicate higher digital literacy. Ege Education Journal 2017(18) 1: 408-429 Digital Literacy Scale: Turkish Adaptation Study 422 Discussion and Conclusion
With the digital age and new technologies, the concept of digital literacy has come to the forefront, and it is considered important for individuals to be digitally literate. In this context, the study aimed to adapt the 17-item “Digital Literacy Scale” developed by Ng (2012) into Turkish. The original scale, which has a four-factor structure, consists of attitude, technical, cognitive, and social dimensions. The scale uses a 5-point Likert-type rating, ranging from Strongly Agree (5) to Strongly Disagree (1), and does not include any reverse-scored items. In the study, linguistic equivalence was initially established: the scale was translated from English to Turkish by three experts fluent in both languages, and from Turkish to English by another three experts. Based on the suggestions of these experts, a Turkish trial form was created and both forms were administered to 37 academics fluent in both English and Turkish at an interval of two weeks. The correlation coefficients between the two forms were found to be .89 for the entire scale, .80 for the Attitude subscale, .93 for the Technical subscale, .73 for the Cognitive subscale, .73 for the Social subscale, and above .30 and significant for all items present in both forms. Once it was determined that the Turkish and English forms of the scale were linguistically equivalent, the construct validity of the scale was examined using EFA and CFA. For the EFA, the suitability of data obtained from 185 students for factor analysis was assessed using the KMO sample adequacy coefficient (.91) and Barlett's Sphericity test value (1549.40, p<.001, df=136), which were found to indicate excellent suitability. The EFA, using the principal components method and varimax rotation, yielded a four-factor structure that explained 65.78% of the total variance and matched the items of the original form exactly. The Attitude subscale consists of 7 items, the Technical subscale consists of 6 items, the Cognitive subscale consists of 2 items, and the Social subscale consists of 2 items. The Attitude subscale accounts for 10.52% of the total variance, the Technical subscale accounts for 44.04%, the Cognitive subscale for 6%, and the Social subscale for 5.22%. The factor loadings range from .31 to .83 for Attitude, .67 to .80 for Technical, .40 and .67 for Cognitive, and .51 and .92 for Social subscales. 

The CFA was conducted with data from 210 students to determine whether the original factor structure of the DLS would be confirmed in the Turkish sample. To assess the adequacy of the model tested in the CFA, fit indices were examined and found as follows: χ2=268.45 (df=113, p=0.00), RMSEA=.071, GFI=.93, AGFI=.91, CFI=.98, NFI=.96, NNFI=.97, and SRMR=.05. These results indicate that the original factor structure of the scale was confirmed in the Turkish sample. Regarding the four-dimensional model obtained from the first-order CFA, factor loadings ranged from .54 to .75 for the “Attitude” subscale, .63 to .79 for the “Technical” subscale, .60 to .69 for the “Cognitive” subscale, and .61 to .77 for the “Social” subscale. The t values ranged from 8.70 to 15.44 and were significant at the .01 level. The number of participants in the research group was found to be sufficient for factor analysis in the first-order CFA. The second-order CFA was conducted to determine to what extent the subscales fit under the higher-order “Digital Literacy” latent variable. As a result of the analysis, the fit indices were χ2=286.60 (df=115, p=0.00), RMSEA=.074, GFI=.96, AGFI=.92, CFI=.97, NFI=.96, NNFI=.97, and SRMR=.048, all of which were at an adequate level. Accordingly, it can be said that digital literacy can be measured as a four-factor structure named Attitude, Technical, Cognitive, and Social. The fit indices obtained from the first and second-order CFA indicate that the construct validity of the Turkish form of the DLS has been established. In addition, all t values were found to be significant at the .01 level; the Attitude, Technical, Cognitive, and Social subscales were determined to be significant predictors of the latent Digital Literacy variable.

The fact that the DLS provides sufficient fit indices in both first and second-order CFA shows that, in addition to allowing for calculations based on the scores from the subscales, a total score for digital literacy can also be obtained from the scale overall. High scores on the subscales and the overall scale indicate a high level of digital literacy.

In the study, convergent and discriminant validity of the scale were examined, and the findings showed that the convergent and discriminant validity of the scale were within an appropriate range. The reliability of the DLS was assessed using the internal consistency coefficient (Cronbach Alpha) and the test-retest methods. The internal consistency coefficient calculated from 185 students was found to be .93 for the entire scale, .88 for the Attitude subscale, .89 for the Technical subscale, .70 for the Cognitive subscale, and .72 for the Social subscale. For test-retest reliability, the correlations between two administrations conducted three weeks apart among 53 students in the computer education and instructional technology department were calculated as .98 for the entire scale, .89 for the Attitude subscale, .90 for the Technical subscale, .87 for the Cognitive subscale, and .79 for the Social subscale. The results indicate that the DLS has adequate reliability coefficients for the entire scale and its subscales. 

The findings obtained in the study provide evidence for the validity and reliability of the DLS, which was developed by Ng (2012) and adapted into Turkish. Due to the lack of sufficient measurement tools for assessing digital literacy skills and the increasing importance of digital literacy skills today, the DLS is a scale that can be used in future research. For upcoming studies, it is recommended that the DLS—which has adequate evidence of validity and reliability—be administered by ensuring measurement invariance across different samples. In this way, the findings obtained from different samples regarding digital literacy skills, which hold significant importance today, will provide support for advancing this area. References

Bu çalışmada Ng tarafından 2012 yılında geliştirilen 17 maddeden oluşan “Dijital Okuryazarlık Ölçeğinin” Türkçe ’ye uyarlaması yapılmıştır. Ölçeğin orijinali 4 faktörlü bir yapıya sahiptir. Bu faktörler tutum, teknik, bilişsel ve sosyal olarak isimlendirilmiştir. Ölçeğin Türkçe’ ye uyarlama çalışmaları dilsel eşdeğerlik ile başlamış, iyi derecede İngilizce ve Türkçe bilen 3 uzman tarafından İngilizce'den Türkçe'ye, farklı 3 uzman tarafından da Türkçe'den İngilizce'ye çevrilmiş, uzmanların görüşleri doğrultusunda Türkçe deneme formu elde edilerek İngilizce ve Türkçe bilen 37 akademisyene iki hafta arayla her iki form uygulanmış ve her iki form arasındaki korelasyon katsayıları anlamlı olarak bulunmuştur. Dilsel eşdeğerliğin ardından AFA, DFA ve güvenirlik analizleri ile gerçekleştirilmiştir. AFA için 185 öğrenciden elde edilen veriler, DFA için ise farklı 210 öğrenciden elde edilen veriler kullanılmıştır. Birinci düzey DFA ile araştırma grubundaki kişi sayısı faktör analizi için yeterli seviyede olduğu, ikinci düzey DFA ile dijital okuryazarlık örtük değişkenin anlamlı birer yordayıcısı olduğu bulunmuştur. İç tutarlılık katsayısı (Cronbach Alpha) ve test tekrar test yöntemleriyle de ölçeğin güvenirliğine bakılmıştır. Elde edilen bulgular sonucunda ölçeğin Türkçe formunun geçerli ve güvenilir bir yapıya sahip olduğu görülmüştür.

In this study, the adaptation of the “Digital Literacy Scale,” developed by Ng in 2012 and consisting of 17 items, into Turkish was carried out. The original scale has a four-factor structure. These factors are named as attitude, technical, cognitive, and social. The adaptation process into Turkish began with linguistic equivalence; three experts who were highly proficient in both English and Turkish translated the scale from English to Turkish, and another three experts translated it from Turkish to English. Based on the experts’ opinions, a Turkish trial form was created, and both the English and Turkish versions were administered to 37 academics proficient in both languages, with two weeks between each administration. The correlation coefficients between the two forms were found to be significant. After establishing linguistic equivalence, EFA, CFA, and reliability analyses were conducted. Data obtained from 185 students were used for EFA, and data from a separate group of 210 students were used for CFA. The first-order CFA showed that the sample size was sufficient for factor analysis, and the second-order CFA demonstrated that digital literacy is a significant predictor of the latent variables. The reliability of the scale was assessed using internal consistency coefficients (Cronbach's Alpha) and test-retest methods. As a result of the findings, it was observed that the Turkish form of the scale has a valid and reliable structure.

discourses.translated_txt: Ege Education Journal 2017(18) 1: 408–429 Digital Literacy Scale: Adaptation to Turkish 411 Digital literacy is one of the essential dimensions that constitute the most important pillar of digital citizenship (Ribble, 2011). There are efforts to define the skills that digital environment users should possess (Burnett and McKinley, 1998; Zins, 2000). Digital literacy requires possessing the skills to use various technologies correctly, to access, produce, and share accurate information, and to utilize technology in learning and teaching processes. Çubukçu and Bayzan (2013) consider the significance of digital literacy skills in that the FATIH Project will hold an important place in the school education process, and that the introduction of the Media Literacy course as an elective in schools is regarded as an opportunity.

discourses.translated_txt: Considering the technological developments experienced, it is observed that there is a need for a measurement tool to determine the level of digital literacy skills in our country. To serve this purpose, it is planned to adapt the digital literacy scale developed by Ng (2012) into our language and culture. For 21st-century individuals, digital literacy skills such as accessing reliable information, safe internet use, and conscious internet use are considered important.

discourses.translated_txt: In the literature, there are studies related to conducting reading and writing using digital technologies as well as studies that highlight the importance of digital literacy in higher education (Özbay and Özdemir, 2014; Prior, Mazanov, Meacheam, Heaslip, and Hanson, 2016; Radovanović, Hogan, and Lalić, 2015; Tüzel and Tok, 2013). Sönmez and Gül (2014) emphasize that in order for individuals to solve the digital problems they encounter in the digital age, they need to possess cognitive skills of digital literacy. Çubukçu and Bayzan (2013) state that digital literacy has begun to become even more important than conventional literacy. In light of these studies, the skills of teachers, who are responsible for imparting digital literacy abilities in education, gain significant importance.

discourses.translated_txt: Statistics on prospective teachers’ access to the internet and their purposes for using it in Türkiye indicate that the vast majority of prospective teachers (86.9%) use the internet (Akkoyunlu and Yılmaz, 2005; Atav, Akkoyunlu, and Sağlam, 2006). Despite this intensive use of the internet, the absence of a measurement tool to reveal prospective teachers’ digital literacy skills makes this study significant. In this study, the adaptation of the Digital Literacy Scale into Turkish is considered important, as it will serve not only to determine the digital literacy skills of prospective teachers but also to provide a basis for activities aimed at developing these skills.

discourses.translated_txt:
Method
Study Group
The validity and reliability studies of the Digital Literacy Scale were conducted during the Spring semester of the 2015-2016 academic year with students from different departments of the Faculty of Education at Sakarya University. Although the sample of the study consisted of four different working groups, a total of 485 individuals participated. The first group consisted of 37 academics—20 (54%) women and 17 (46%) men—and linguistic equivalence studies were conducted with this group. The second group comprised 185 people—108 (58.4%) women and 77 (41.6%) men—and data from this group were used for exploratory factor analysis and internal consistency studies. The third group consisted of 210 people—118 (56.2%) women and 92 (43.8%) men—and confirmatory factor analysis results were obtained from this group. The fourth group included 53 people—20 (37.7%) women and 33 (62.3%) men—and test-retest analyses of the scale were conducted using data obtained from this group.

Dijital Okuryazarlık Ölçeği (DOYÖ) Ng (2012) tarafından geliştirilmiş 17 maddeden ve 4 faktörden
(tutum, teknik, bilişsel ve sosyal) oluşan bir ölçektir. Ölçeğin orijinali Avustralya’da bulunan bir
üniversitede öğrenim gören, yaşları 18 ile 30 arasında değişen öğretmen adayları üzerinde
uygulanmıştır. Tersten puanlanan maddenin bulunmadığı ölçekte Kesinlikle Katılıyorum (5),
Kesinlikle Katılmıyorum (1) şeklinde 5’li Likert tipi bir derecelendirme kullanılmıştır. İşlem
Dijital Okuryazarlık Ölçeğinin Türkçeye uyarlama çalışması öncelikle orijinal dilde ölçeğin
geliştiricisi olan Ng ile iletişime geçilerek ölçeğin uyarlanması için izin alınmasıyla
başlamıştır. Gerekli izinler sağlandıktan sonra ölçeğin kaynak dil olan İngilizceden hedef dil
olan Türkçeye çeviri süreci başlatılmıştır. Bir ölçme aracının geliştirildiği toplumdan farklı
bir topluma uyarlanması sırasındaki en önemli işlemi ölçeğin kaynak dilden hedef dile
çevirisi süreci oluşturmaktadır (Geisinger, 1994). Her iki formun yeteri kadar birbirine
benzediği görüşü alındıktan sonra ölçeğin uygulama hazır, son hali ortaya çıkarılmıştır. Ölçek
dil geçerliliği için yeterli hale getirilmiştir. Dilsel eşdeğerliliği çalışmaları 37 akademisyen ile
Ege Eğitim Dergisi 2017(18) 1: 408- 429 Dijital Okuryazarlık Ölçeği: Türkçe ’ye Uyarlama Çalışması 413 iki dilli desen yöntemiyle yürütülmüştür. Yapı geçerliliği için toplanan veri, veri ön işleme
yöntemleri kullanılarak incelenmiştir (Oğuzlar, 2003). DOYÖ’nin yapı geçerliliği çalışması
betimleyici faktör analizi (exploratory factor analysis) ve doğrulayıcı faktör analizi
(confirmatory factor analysis) yöntemleri kullanılarak yürütülmüştür. Faktör analizi
çalışmalarında bazı varsayımsal ölçütlerin aranması gerekmektedir. Bu amaçla varsayımsal
ölçütler olarak AFA için normal dağılım, doğrusallık, aykırı değerlerin çıkarılması, boş
değerlerin belirlenmesi incelenirken DFA için aranan tüm varsayımsal kriterlerle birlikte
uyum iyiliği indekslerinin yeterlilik düzeyleri incelenmiştir. DOYÖ’nin uyarlama çalışmasında toplanan verinin yapı geçerliği çalışmaları için
gereken yeterliliği gösterdiği gözlenerek yapı geçerliği çalışması yapılmıştır. Ölçeğin
güvenirlik düzeyi Cronbach alfa iç tutarlılık ve test tekrar test yöntemleri aracılığıyla
incelenmiştir. DOYÖ’nin uyarlama çalışmalarında kullanılan tüm istatistiksel analizler SPSS
20.0 ve LISREL 8.7 paket programlarıyla yapılmıştır.
discourses.translated_txt:
Data Collection Tool: Digital Literacy Scale  
The Digital Literacy Scale (DLS) was developed by Ng (2012) and consists of 17 items and 4 factors (attitude, technical, cognitive, and social). The original scale was administered to prospective teachers aged between 18 and 30 studying at a university in Australia. The scale does not contain any reverse-scored items and uses a 5-point Likert scale ranging from Strongly Agree (5) to Strongly Disagree (1).  
Procedure  
The process of adapting the Digital Literacy Scale into Turkish began with obtaining permission to adapt the scale from its developer, Ng, in the original language. Once the necessary permissions were obtained, the translation process from the source language, English, to the target language, Turkish, was initiated. The most important step in adapting a measurement tool from one society to another is the translation process from the source language to the target language (Geisinger, 1994). After it was confirmed that both versions were sufficiently similar, the final draft of the scale became ready for implementation. The scale was made adequate for language validity. Linguistic equivalence studies were carried out using the bilingual design method with 37 academicians.  
For construct validity, the collected data were examined using data preprocessing methods (Oğuzlar, 2003). The construct validity study of the DLS was conducted using exploratory factor analysis (EFA) and confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) methods. Certain hypothetical criteria are required for factor analysis studies. For this purpose, in EFA, assumptions such as normality, linearity, removal of outliers, and identification of missing values were examined, while in CFA, all required hypothetical criteria were investigated along with the adequacy levels of goodness-of-fit indices.  
It was observed that the data collected for the adaptation study of the DLS met the requisite adequacy for construct validity, and thus, a construct validity study was conducted. The reliability level of the scale was examined using Cronbach's alpha internal consistency and test-retest methods. All statistical analyses used in the adaptation studies of the DLS were conducted using the SPSS 20.0 and LISREL 8.7 software packages.

Açımlayıcı Faktör Analizi (AFA)
Açımlayıcı faktör analizi gerçekleştirilmeden önce veri setinin faktör analizi için uygun olup
olmadığının belirlenmesi gerekir. Örneklemin veri analizine uygun olup olmadığını
belirlemek için yapılacak işlem Kaiser-Meyer-Oklin’in (KMO) ve Barlett Sphericity
testlerinin gerçekleştirilmesidir. KMO 0 ile 1 arasında değişen değerler alabilmektedir ve
0.5’in üzerindeki KMO değerleri kabul edilebilir değerdir (Field, 2009). Bununla birlikte; 0.5
ile 0.7 arasındaki KMO değerlerinin orta, 0.7 ile 0.8 arasındaki değerlerin iyi, 0.8 ile 0.9
arasındaki değerlerin çok iyi ve 0.9’un üzerindeki değerlerin ise mükemmel olduğu kabul
edilmektedir (Field, 2009). Bu çalışmada KMO örneklem uygunluk katsayısı .91, Barlett
Sphericity testi değeri ise 1549.40 (p<.01, sd=136) bulunmuştur. Bu sonuca göre, verilerin
faktör analizine mükemmel uygunlukta olduğu söylenebilir. AFA’da temel bileşenler
yöntemi (principal components) ve varimax döndürme tekniği kullanılmıştır. Temel
bileşenler yöntemi bağımlılık yapısını yok etme amacıyla tanıma, sınıflandırma, boyut
indirgenme ve yorumlanmasını sağlayan, çok değişkenli bir istatistiksel yöntemdir (Jolliffe,
2002). Buna göre AFA sonucunda toplam varyansın %65.78’ini açıklayan ve orijinal
formdaki maddelerle bire bir örtüşen 4 faktörlü bir yapı elde edilmiştir (Şekil 1).
discourses.translated_txt:
Exploratory Factor Analysis (EFA)
Before conducting exploratory factor analysis, it is necessary to determine whether the data set is suitable for factor analysis. The procedures to determine whether the sample is appropriate for data analysis are the implementation of the Kaiser-Meyer-Olkin (KMO) and Bartlett’s Sphericity tests. The KMO can take values ranging from 0 to 1, and KMO values above 0.5 are considered acceptable (Field, 2009). Moreover, KMO values between 0.5 and 0.7 are considered moderate, values between 0.7 and 0.8 are considered good, values between 0.8 and 0.9 are considered very good, and values over 0.9 are regarded as excellent (Field, 2009). In this study, the KMO sample adequacy coefficient was found to be .91, and the Bartlett’s Sphericity test value was 1549.40 (p<.01, df=136). According to these results, it can be said that the data are in excellent conformity for factor analysis. In EFA, the principal components method and varimax rotation technique were used. The principal components method is a multivariate statistical technique that enables identification, classification, dimensionality reduction, and interpretation, and aims to remove the dependence structure (Jolliffe, 2002). Accordingly, as a result of the EFA, a four-factor structure was obtained that accounts for 65.78% of the total variance and exactly matches the items in the original form (Figure 1).

discourses.translated_txt:
In the study, linguistic equivalence was initially established: the scale was translated from English to Turkish by three experts fluent in both languages, and from Turkish to English by another three experts. Based on the suggestions of these experts, a Turkish trial form was created and both forms were administered to 37 academics fluent in both English and Turkish at an interval of two weeks. The correlation coefficients between the two forms were found to be .89 for the entire scale, .80 for the Attitude subscale, .93 for the Technical subscale, .73 for the Cognitive subscale, .73 for the Social subscale, and above .30 and significant for all items present in both forms. Once it was determined that the Turkish and English forms of the scale were linguistically equivalent, the construct validity of the scale was examined using EFA and CFA. For the EFA, the suitability of data obtained from 185 students for factor analysis was assessed using the KMO sample adequacy coefficient (.91) and Barlett's Sphericity test value (1549.40, p<.001, df=136), which were found to indicate excellent suitability. The EFA, using the principal components method and varimax rotation, yielded a four-factor structure that explained 65.78% of the total variance and matched the items of the original form exactly. The Attitude subscale consists of 7 items, the Technical subscale consists of 6 items, the Cognitive subscale consists of 2 items, and the Social subscale consists of 2 items. The Attitude subscale accounts for 10.52% of the total variance, the Technical subscale accounts for 44.04%, the Cognitive subscale for 6%, and the Social subscale for 5.22%. The factor loadings range from .31 to .83 for Attitude, .67 to .80 for Technical, .40 and .67 for Cognitive, and .51 and .92 for Social subscales. 

The CFA was conducted with data from 210 students to determine whether the original factor structure of the DLS would be confirmed in the Turkish sample. To assess the adequacy of the model tested in the CFA, fit indices were examined and found as follows: χ2=268.45 (df=113, p=0.00), RMSEA=.071, GFI=.93, AGFI=.91, CFI=.98, NFI=.96, NNFI=.97, and SRMR=.05. These results indicate that the original factor structure of the scale was confirmed in the Turkish sample. Regarding the four-dimensional model obtained from the first-order CFA, factor loadings ranged from .54 to .75 for the “Attitude” subscale, .63 to .79 for the “Technical” subscale, .60 to .69 for the “Cognitive” subscale, and .61 to .77 for the “Social” subscale. The t values ranged from 8.70 to 15.44 and were significant at the .01 level. The number of participants in the research group was found to be sufficient for factor analysis in the first-order CFA. The second-order CFA was conducted to determine to what extent the subscales fit under the higher-order “Digital Literacy” latent variable. As a result of the analysis, the fit indices were χ2=286.60 (df=115, p=0.00), RMSEA=.074, GFI=.96, AGFI=.92, CFI=.97, NFI=.96, NNFI=.97, and SRMR=.048, all of which were at an adequate level. Accordingly, it can be said that digital literacy can be measured as a four-factor structure named Attitude, Technical, Cognitive, and Social. The fit indices obtained from the first and second-order CFA indicate that the construct validity of the Turkish form of the DLS has been established. In addition, all t values were found to be significant at the .01 level; the Attitude, Technical, Cognitive, and Social subscales were determined to be significant predictors of the latent Digital Literacy variable.

The fact that the DLS provides sufficient fit indices in both first and second-order CFA shows that, in addition to allowing for calculations based on the scores from the subscales, a total score for digital literacy can also be obtained from the scale overall. High scores on the subscales and the overall scale indicate a high level of digital literacy.

In the study, convergent and discriminant validity of the scale were examined, and the findings showed that the convergent and discriminant validity of the scale were within an appropriate range. The reliability of the DLS was assessed using the internal consistency coefficient (Cronbach Alpha) and the test-retest methods. The internal consistency coefficient calculated from 185 students was found to be .93 for the entire scale, .88 for the Attitude subscale, .89 for the Technical subscale, .70 for the Cognitive subscale, and .72 for the Social subscale. For test-retest reliability, the correlations between two administrations conducted three weeks apart among 53 students in the computer education and instructional technology department were calculated as .98 for the entire scale, .89 for the Attitude subscale, .90 for the Technical subscale, .87 for the Cognitive subscale, and .79 for the Social subscale. The results indicate that the DLS has adequate reliability coefficients for the entire scale and its subscales. 

The findings obtained in the study provide evidence for the validity and reliability of the DLS, which was developed by Ng (2012) and adapted into Turkish.

discourses.translated_txt: Due to the lack of sufficient measurement tools for assessing digital literacy skills and the increasing importance of digital literacy skills today, the DLS is a scale that can be used in future research. For upcoming studies, it is recommended that the DLS—which has adequate evidence of validity and reliability—be administered by ensuring measurement invariance across different samples. In this way, the findings obtained from different samples regarding digital literacy skills, which hold significant importance today, will provide support for advancing this area.
